docs.title: What is it and what can I do with it
docs.text:
DynamicForms is a client library to automate Progressive Filtering and the initialisation of dynamic fields in an easy and fast way.

It supports the developer in managing and centralizing all forms interactions.

It's written in typescript and built with tsdown

Here's some examples.

docs.title: Automatic fields initialisation with remote options
docs.text: The Progressive Filtering chain is restored: all the available options are automatically fetched.

docs.title: Visibility changes depending on fields' values
Much much more
docs.text: Got your attention? Try it!

docs.title: Main features
docs.text:
• Easy to use: DynamicForms works in a declarative way; no code for the standard behaviour, just a simple configuration!
  • Modern javascript: works on Chrome and Edge 111+, Firefox 114+ and Safari 16.4+, with no polyfills
  • Lightweight: having no dependencies, you can integrate it everywhere!
  • Automate repetitive and boring operations: read values, fetch data making async remote calls, update fields' status, clear other fields, hide/show sections... even listing them is BORING!
  • Highly customizable: are you using an external library with custom html elements? Don't worry as you can specify your own functions to read/write data

docs.text:

If you have questions or suggestions open an issue on github.

Thank you very much for your support ❤

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
DynamicForms is designed to be simple and straightforward - no complex setup or configuration required.

The library offers 2 main functions that handle all the heavy lifting for you, including completing the Form Configuration with defaults and the form initialisation.

For 90% of use cases, makeForm is all you need!

First, import the module (see loading guide)

import { makeForm, getForm } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';

docs.title: TypeScript
docs.text:
The package exports the configuration types, so Form and Field Configurations can be written in their own files without casts. Only the form id is required, the library completes the rest.

import { makeForm, type FormConfiguration, type FieldConfiguration } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';

const city: FieldConfiguration = {
    name: 'city',
    fetch: { makeUrl: (data) => `/cities?country=${data.country}` },
    select: { clearOnParentVoid: false },
};
const configuration: FormConfiguration = {
    id: 'checkout',
    fields: [city],
    rules: [{ name: 'country', update: ['city'] }],
    behavior: { afterInit: () => console.log('ready') },
};
makeForm(configuration);

Exported types: FormConfiguration, FormHooks, UpdateRule, InitialisationRule, FieldConfiguration, FieldIoHooks, FieldFetchConfiguration, FieldHooks, SelectConfiguration, SelectOption, CheckboxConfiguration, FieldElement, UpdateData and DynamicForm (a type only: forms are created by makeForm). The package also exports the RemoteCallError class, the error of a failed remote call.

docs.title: makeForm (formConfiguration)
docs.text:
Creates a form. An html form has at most one Form at a time: makeForm throws Form "id" already exists when the previous Form for that id has not been destroyed (see destroy).

Parameters

  • {object} formConfiguration: the Form Configuration

Returns

  • {DynamicForm} the form

docs.title: getForm (id)
docs.text:
Returns the form with the given id, if it exists.

Parameters

  • {string} id: the form id

Returns

  • {DynamicForm | null} the form, or null if it does not exist

docs.title: destroy ()
docs.text:
A method of the Form returned by makeForm. It removes the Form's listeners, so the fields no longer update each other, unregisters it from getForm, and aborts its remote calls in progress. Destroying it again does nothing.

A notify(), manualUpdate() or ready() still pending rejects with Form "id" was destroyed, and so do notify() and manualUpdate() called afterwards. A custom updateStatus Field Hook receives the abort signal, to stop its own remote calls.

docs.title: Fields added after makeForm
docs.text:
Fields are discovered when the Form is created. To pick up fields added to the html form later, destroy the Form and create it again:

let form = makeForm(configuration);
// ...the page adds <input name="notes"> to the form...
form.destroy();
form = makeForm(configuration);

The new Form runs the Initialisation again, so its Initialisation Rules set the initial Values again. To keep the Values the user has changed meanwhile, create it without them:

form.destroy();
form = makeForm({ ...configuration, init: [] });

docs.title: Field Configuration
docs.text:
This document describes a single Field Configuration. The list of Field Configurations goes in the fields section of the Form Configuration.

Just specify the fields you want to customise: the other ones are discovered and added to the form automatically, with the standard behaviour.

Every Field Hook receives htmlElement as the NodeList of all the html elements with the field name, even when there is only one: read a single input with htmlElement[0].value.

A Field Hook which replaces a Standard Behaviour of the field (listening, reading, writing, clearing, updating its status, loading and saving a select's options) receives it as its last parameter, standard: call it to run the Standard Behaviour and add to it, instead of rewriting it. It takes no arguments and works on the hook's own ones.

select: {
    saveData: (htmlElement, data, standard) => {
        standard(); // writes the <option>s as usual
        htmlElement[0].dispatchEvent(new Event('options-saved'));
    },
}

To integrate a third-party widget (select2, Choices.js, a date picker...), see Third-party widgets.

!!! tip "TypeScript" TypeScript cannot see the html, so Field Hooks receive a NodeListOf<HTMLInputElement | HTMLSelectElement | HTMLTextAreaElement> and an any value. State the element and value types on the field to use them without casts:

```typescript
import type { FieldConfiguration } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';

const city: FieldConfiguration<HTMLSelectElement> = {
    name: 'city',
    behavior: { clear: (htmlElement) => { htmlElement[0].options.length = 0; } },
};
const tags: FieldConfiguration<HTMLInputElement, string[]> = {
    name: 'tags',
    io: {
        get: (htmlElement) => htmlElement[0].value.split(','),
        set: (htmlElement, value) => { htmlElement[0].value = value.join(','); },
    },
};
```

The element type can be any `HTMLElement`, such as a form-associated custom element (see [Third-party widgets](./third-party-widgets.md#custom-elements)). The `standard` parameter of each hook is typed too: in `tags` above, `io.get`'s `standard` returns `string[]`.

The library does not check these types against the html: `FieldConfiguration<HTMLSelectElement>` on an `<input>` compiles but fails at runtime.

Here's a complete Field Configuration. You just need to specify the attributes you need, the other will have default values.

Generic fieldSelect fieldCheckbox field 
const fieldConfiguration = {
    name: 'fieldName',
    io: {  // Customize field input/output
        event: 'change',
        listen: (htmlElement, onChange, standard) => { return () => { }; }, // Subscribe to the field's changes, return the unsubscribe function
        get: (htmlElement, standard) => { },
        set: (htmlElement, value, standard) => { },
    },
    fetch: { // Remote call options
        method: 'GET',
        makeUrl: (data) => { },
        makeBody: (data) => { }, // JSON.stringify, formData, text...
        fullFetchConfig: (data) => { }, // Fetch complete configuration (RequestInit)
    },
    behavior: { // Field Hooks
        clear: (htmlElement, standard) => { }, // Clear the field's value
        beforeUpdate: (htmlElement, data, subjectName) => { return true; }, // Executed before the remote call. Return false to block the update
        updateStatus: (htmlElement, data, subjectName, signal, standard) => { },
        afterUpdate: (htmlElement, data, subjectName) => { } // Executed after the remote call
    }
};

const fieldConfiguration = {
    name: 'fieldName',
    io: /* ... */,
    fetch: /* ... */,
    behavior: /* ... */,
    select: { // Only for select fields
        loadOptions: (htmlElement, data, subjectName, signal, standard) => { }, // Load the data instead of the remote call
        postProcessData: (htmlElement, data, standard) => { }, // Process data retrieved by the remote call or loadOptions
        saveData: (htmlElement, data, standard) => { }, // Manually save data in html (e.g. creating `<option value="value">'text'</option>` nodes)
        clearOnParentVoid: true, // True (default) to clear the field when the Subject's value is empty; false to trigger a remote call
    }
};

const fieldConfiguration = {
    name: 'fieldName',
    io: /* ... */,
    fetch: /* ... */,
    behavior: /* ... */,
    checkbox: { // Only for checkbox fields
        booleanValue: true // True (default) to get the field's value as boolean, based on the checked property; false to get the value property
    }
};

docs.title: name*
docs.text:
The field name: the name attribute of its html elements.

Type: string.

required

docs.title: io
docs.text: Object which groups the properties to read and write the field's value.

docs.title: event
docs.text:
The html event which signals that the field's value changed (e.g. change for a select, click for a checkbox...).

The library listens to it to update the Observers of the field when it is a Subject, unless a listen Field Hook replaces the listening.

Type: string.

Default value: change.

docs.title: listen (htmlElement, onChange, standard)
docs.text:
Field Hook which replaces the standard listening to the field's changes: it subscribes to them, calls onChange on each one, and returns the function which unsubscribes. The library calls that function when the Form is destroyed.

Use it for a widget which announces its changes in a way addEventListener doesn't hear, such as jQuery events or a callback:

io: {
    listen: (htmlElement, onChange) => {
        $(htmlElement).on('change.dynamicForms', onChange);
        return () => $(htmlElement).off('change.dynamicForms');
    },
}

While the library writes to the field (set, clear, saveData), it ignores the field's changes: a widget which fires change when written by code doesn't start a second update of the Observers, which the library already updates.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {() => void} onChange: to call on each change of the field
  • {() => () => void} standard: listens to event on the html nodes, and returns the function which stops

Returns

  • {() => void} the function which unsubscribes

docs.title: get (htmlElement, standard)
docs.text:
Function to read the field's value. Useful for custom html elements.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {() => any} standard: reads the value the way the library does for this kind of field

Returns

  • {string} the field's value

docs.title: set (htmlElement, value, standard)
docs.text:
Function to write the field's value. Useful for custom html elements.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {mixed} value: the field's new value
  • {() => void} standard: writes value the way the library does for this kind of field

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: fetch*
docs.text:
Object which groups properties related to remote calls.

Available only for select fields.

Required only if the select field is an Observer (it is updated on every change of its Subject), unless you specify a loadOptions or an updateStatus Field Hook.

When the remote call answers with a non-ok status, notify() (or ready(), during the Initialisation) rejects with a RemoteCallError, an Error exported by the package whose response holds the Response:

import { RemoteCallError } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';

try {
    await form.notify('country');
} catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof RemoteCallError) {
        console.log(error.message);          // Remote call to "/regions" failed with status 404
        console.log(error.response.status);  // 404
    }
}

docs.title: method
docs.text:
It's the http request method (or verb).

Type: string.

Default value: GET

docs.title: makeUrl (data)*
docs.text:
A function to generate the url to make the remote call to.

required

Parameters

  • {JSON} data: the Update Data

Returns

  • {string} The remote call url

docs.title: makeBody (data)
docs.text:
A function to generate the remote call body in the desired method (e.g. JSON.stringify, FormData...).

It's not necessary if the remote call uses the GET request method (the Update Data needs to be placed in the url).

Parameters

  • {JSON} data: the Update Data

Returns

  • {object} The remote call body

docs.title: fullFetchConfig (data)
docs.text:
A function to generate the complete Fetch configuration for remote calls.

Use it when the request needs more than a method and a body, e.g. headers that depend on the field values.

If this function is defined, the standard update ignores the fetch.method property and the fetch.makeBody function.

Parameters

  • {JSON} data: the Update Data

Returns

  • {RequestInit} The complete Fetch configuration, passed as is to fetch as its second argument
fetch: {
    makeUrl: (data) => '/posts',
    fullFetchConfig: (data) => ({
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify(data),
    }),
}

Until 3.x fullFetchConfig was a static object. Since 4.0.0 it must be a function: wrap an existing object as fullFetchConfig: () => ({ ... }).

docs.title: behavior
docs.text: Object which groups the Field Hooks.

docs.title: clear (htmlElement, standard)
docs.text:
Field Hook which replaces the standard clear: it empties the field of its value (and, for a select, of its options).

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {() => void} standard: clears the field the way the library does for this kind of field

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: beforeUpdate (htmlElement, data, subjectName)
docs.text:
Field Hook called before the field's update. If it returns false, the update is aborted.

Default: nothing. It adds to the field's standard behaviour without switching any of it off: a select whose Subject's value is empty is cleared, and this hook is not called (see clearOnParentVoid).

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {JSON} data: the Update Data
  • {string | null}: subjectName: the name of the Subject which triggered the update. It is null for a manual update

Returns

  • {boolean} false to abort the update, true otherwise

docs.title: updateStatus (htmlElement, data, subjectName, signal, standard)
docs.text:
Field Hook which replaces the standard update of the field's status: its attributes (display, disabled...) and, for a select, its options.

Default: nothing. For select fields it makes a remote call (using fetch), retrieves the new data and saves it as the select's new options.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {JSON} data: the Update Data
  • {string | null}: subjectName: the name of the Subject which triggered the update. It is null for a manual update
  • {AbortSignal}: signal: aborted when the Form is destroyed. Pass it to the hook's remote calls (fetch(url, { signal })) so they stop with the Form
  • {() => Promise<void>}: standard: updates the status the way the library does: nothing, or for a select its remote call and the saving of the options

Returns

  • {Promise<void>}

docs.title: afterUpdate (htmlElement, data, subjectName)
docs.text:
Field Hook called after the field's update, also when the update was aborted.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {JSON} data: the Update Data
  • {string | null}: subjectName: the name of the Subject which triggered the update. It is null for a manual update

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: select
docs.text:
Object which groups properties related to select fields.

A select updates its options in three steps, each replaceable by a Field Hook:

remote call (or loadOptions) → postProcessData → saveData

docs.title: loadOptions (htmlElement, data, subjectName, signal, standard)
docs.text:
Field Hook which replaces the remote call: it loads the data another way (another http client, a cache, data already in the page) and the update goes on as usual, through postProcessData and saveData. With it, fetch is not needed.

select: {
    loadOptions: async (htmlElement, data, subjectName, signal) =>
        (await axios.get('/regions', { params: { country: data.country }, signal })).data,
    postProcessData: (htmlElement, regions) => regions.map(r => ({ value: r.id, text: r.name })),
}

Parameters (the same as updateStatus)

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {JSON} data: the Update Data
  • {string | null}: subjectName: the name of the Subject which triggered the update. It is null for a manual update
  • {AbortSignal}: signal: aborted when the Form is destroyed
  • {() => Promise<any>}: standard: makes the remote call with fetch, and resolves with the response parsed as json

Returns

  • {any | Promise<any>} the data which postProcessData receives, or directly the options when there is no postProcessData

docs.title: postProcessData (htmlElement, data, standard)
docs.text:
Field Hook to process the data retrieved by the remote call or by loadOptions. It is useful for filtering/ordering data.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name
  • {JSON} data: data retrieved from the remote call or returned by loadOptions
  • {() => any} standard: returns data as it is

Returns

  • {{ value: string | number, text: string }[]} the options to save

docs.title: saveData (htmlElement, data, standard)
docs.text:
Field Hook which replaces the standard saving of the options: it writes the (post-processed) data retrieved by the remote call or by loadOptions in the html.

Default: saves the data as option html elements using value and text properties, creating also empty option if they are not present in retrieved data.

Parameters

  • {NodeList} htmlElement: the html nodes with the field name, where data will be saved
  • {{ value: string | number, text: string }[]} data: the options returned by postProcessData, or the data retrieved from the remote call or by loadOptions when there is no postProcessData
  • {() => void} standard: saves the options the way the library does

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: clearOnParentVoid
docs.text:
Property which (when true) tells to clear the field when the Subject's value is empty, instead of triggering a remote call (when false).

The clear happens before the beforeUpdate Field Hook, which is then not called: set this property to false to handle an empty Subject's value in the hook.

Type: boolean.

Default value: true.

docs.title: checkbox
docs.text: Object which groups properties related to checkbox fields.

docs.title: booleanValue
docs.text:
Property which tells if the field's value is boolean.

When true the field considers its value as boolean, based on the html checked attribute; when false it considers its value as string, based on the value attribute.

Type: boolean.

Default value: true.

docs.title: Form Configuration
docs.text:
This document describes the complete Form Configuration with focus on each property.

The Form Configuration is written client side and passed to makeForm (see DynamicForms library) to create the form.

Glossary:

  • Subject: the role of a field whose change triggers an Update Rule
  • Observer: the role of a field updated when the Subject of an Update Rule changes. The same field can be Observer in one rule and Subject in another

Here's the complete form configuration:

const formConfiguration = {
    id: 'form_id',
    debug: true,
    behavior: { // Form Hooks
        beforeUpdate: (subjectName) => { }, // Executed before updating the Observers. Return false to block all updates
        afterUpdate: (subjectName) => { }, // Executed after updating the Observers
        beforeInit: () => { }, // Executed before the form initialisation
        afterInit: () => { } // Executed after the form initialisation
    },
    fields: [], // Collection of Field Configurations
    rules: [], // Collection of Update Rules
    init: [] // Collection of Initialisation Rules
};

makeForm checks the configuration before building the form. Every field name it mentions (in fields, rules and init) must be a field of the form; otherwise it throws an error listing every unknown name:

Invalid form configuration "form_id":
- update rule "country": unknown field "regoin" in update
- initialisation rule "contry": unknown field

docs.title: id*
docs.text:
The form id. Just the plain text, no '#'.

Type: string.

required

docs.title: debug
docs.text:
A flag to activate the debug mode which prints in the console every Update Rule and the initialisation right before their execution.

Type: boolean.

docs.title: behavior
docs.text: Object which groups the Form Hooks (e.g. what to do before or after an update).

docs.title: beforeUpdate (subjectName)
docs.text:
Form Hook called after a Subject changes, but before updating its Observers.

Useful to show a loader during the fields update.

Parameters

  • {string} subjectName: the name of the Subject which triggered the update. Manual updates (form.manualUpdate) don't call this Form Hook

Returns

  • {bool} false to abort the update, true otherwise

docs.title: afterUpdate (subjectName)
docs.text:
Form Hook called after all the updated Observers have completed their update.

Useful to hide a loader after the fields update.

Parameters

  • {string} subjectName: the name of the Subject which triggered the update. Manual updates (form.manualUpdate) don't call this Form Hook

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: beforeInit ()
docs.text:
Form Hook called before the form initialisation.

Useful to show a loader before all fields are initialised.

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: afterInit ()
docs.text:
Form Hook called after the form initialisation.

Useful to hide any loader after the form is ready.

Returns

  • {void}

docs.title: fields
docs.text:
A collection of Field Configurations.

Include here the fields you want to customise (get/set/update operations). The other ones are discovered automatically.

See Field Configuration.

docs.title: rules
docs.text:
A collection of Update Rules.

Include here all the rules like "if field A changes, trigger the update of fields B and C".

See Update Rule configuration.

docs.title: init
docs.text:
A collection of Initialisation Rules.

Include here all fields which will be updated when the form is created.

See Initialisation Rule configuration.

docs.title: Single Initialisation Rule configuration
docs.text:
These rules declare the fields to bring up to date when the form is created, optionally with their initial value.

An Initialisation Rule can name a field of the form, or external data which is not a field.

const initialisationRuleConfiguration = {
    name: 'fieldName',
    value: any
};

docs.title: name*
docs.text: The field name.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
The field value. It can be any primitive value.

This attribute has 2 purposes:

  • It's passed in the Update Data of every field listed in the Initialisation Rules;
  • It becomes the field's value; for a select field, the value must be among its options to be selected.

docs.title: Third-party widgets
docs.text:
A widget is a third-party control shown in place of a field's html element, such as select2, Choices.js, Tom Select or a date picker. It keeps the html element in sync, but has its own way of being read, written and listened to.

DynamicForms integrates a widget through the Field Hooks of its field. The field is still the html element with the name (the <select> or <input> the widget decorates or hides), so the widget is created on that element before makeForm.

docs.title: What to write
docs.text:
A widget needs a Field Hook only where the library's Standard Behaviour doesn't fit:

The widget... Field Hook announces its changes with jQuery events or a callback, which addEventListener doesn't hear io.listen announces them with an event other than change io.event doesn't keep the element's value up to date io.get doesn't show a value written in the element io.set doesn't show an emptied element behavior.clear doesn't show the <option>s written in the select select.saveData

A Field Hook which replaces a Standard Behaviour receives it as its last parameter, standard. When the widget only needs to read again what the library wrote, run the standard and refresh it:

select: {
    saveData: (htmlElement, data, standard) => {
        standard(); // writes the <option>s as usual
        $(htmlElement).selectpicker('refresh');
    },
}

Many widgets fire change when written by code. While the library writes to a field (io.set, behavior.clear, select.saveData), it ignores the field's changes, so they don't start a second update of its Observers, which the library already updates. The events still reach the widget and your code.

This covers events fired during the write. A widget which reacts later (after a timeout or a microtask) and then fires change still starts an update: pass it the option that makes it silent.

docs.title: Reusing an integration
docs.text:
A widget's Field Hooks are the same for every field which uses it: write them once in a function returning the field configuration. The recipes below take the field name and the overrides of that field, and merge them section by section with mergeField, so that { fetch: { makeUrl } } adds to the widget's hooks instead of replacing a whole section:

/**
 * Merges a Field Configuration with overrides section by section: in `io`, `fetch`, `behavior`, `select`
 * and `checkbox` the overrides replace only the keys they have, where a plain spread would replace the whole section.
 */
export function mergeField(field, overrides = {}) {
    const merged = { ...field, ...overrides };
    for (const section of ['io', 'fetch', 'behavior', 'select', 'checkbox']) {
        if (field[section] || overrides[section]) {
            merged[section] = { ...field[section], ...overrides[section] };
        }
    }
    return merged;
}

import { select2Field } from './select2.js';

$('select[name="country"], select[name="city"]').select2();
const form = makeForm({
    id: 'address',
    fields: [
        select2Field('country'),
        select2Field('city', { fetch: { makeUrl: (data) => `/cities?country=${data.country}` } }),
    ],
    rules: [{ name: 'country', update: ['city'] }],
});

When the widget's instance can't be reached from the html element, pass it to the function, and the hooks keep it (see Choices.js below).

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Copy and adapt them. They are tested against the widget versions in the notes, except bootstrap-select.

select2Choices.jsTom Selectbootstrap-selectflatpickr

Tested with select2 4.1 and jQuery 4.

import { mergeField } from './merge-field.js';

/**
 * A select Field shown as a select2 Widget (https://select2.org), created before makeForm with `$(select).select2()`.
 * - select2 announces changes only through jQuery events, which addEventListener never hears: io.listen listens with jQuery.
 * - It re-reads the <option>s the library writes by itself, but shows a new Value only after a jQuery `change`.
 */
export function select2Field(name, overrides = {}) {
    return mergeField({
        name,
        io: {
            listen: (htmlElement, onChange) => {
                $(htmlElement).on('change.dynamicForms', onChange);
                return () => $(htmlElement).off('change.dynamicForms');
            },
            set: (htmlElement, value, standard) => {
                standard();
                $(htmlElement).trigger('change');
            },
        },
        behavior: {
            clear: (htmlElement, standard) => {
                standard();
                $(htmlElement).trigger('change');
            },
        },
    }, overrides);
}

Tested with Choices.js 11.

import { mergeField } from './merge-field.js';

/**
 * A select Field shown as a Choices.js Widget (https://choices-js.github.io/Choices/), created before makeForm with `new Choices(select)`.
 * - Its instance can't be reached from the <select>: pass it, and the hooks keep it in their closure.
 * - Choices dispatches a DOM `change` on the <select>, which the Standard Behaviour of io.listen hears.
 * - It doesn't notice the <option>s the library writes: after writing them, `refresh` reads them again.
 */
export function choicesField(name, choices, overrides = {}) {
    return mergeField({
        name,
        io: {
            // With no choice made, the <select> value would be its first option
            get: () => choices.getValue(true) ?? '',
            set: (_htmlElement, value) => {
                choices.setChoiceByValue(value);
            },
        },
        behavior: {
            clear: (_htmlElement, standard) => {
                standard();
                choices.refresh(false, false, true);
            },
        },
        select: {
            saveData: (_htmlElement, _options, standard) => {
                standard();
                choices.refresh(false, false, true);
            },
        },
    }, overrides);
}

const city = new Choices('select[name="city"]');
makeForm({ id: 'address', fields: [choicesField('city', city, { fetch: { makeUrl } })], /* ... */ });

Tested with Tom Select 2.

import { mergeField } from './merge-field.js';

/**
 * A select Field shown as a Tom Select Widget (https://tom-select.js.org), created before makeForm with `new TomSelect(select)`.
 * - Tom Select dispatches DOM `change` events on the <select>, which the Standard Behaviour of io.listen hears.
 * - It keeps its own list of Options: they are written through its api, not as <option>s.
 * - Its writes fire `change`: the library ignores the changes of a field while it writes it.
 */
export function tomSelectField(name, overrides = {}) {
    return mergeField({
        name,
        io: {
            set: (htmlElement, value) => {
                htmlElement[0].tomselect.setValue(value);
            },
        },
        behavior: {
            clear: (htmlElement) => {
                const tomSelect = htmlElement[0].tomselect;
                tomSelect.clear();
                tomSelect.clearOptions();
            },
        },
        select: {
            saveData: (htmlElement, options) => {
                const tomSelect = htmlElement[0].tomselect;
                tomSelect.clear();
                tomSelect.clearOptions();
                tomSelect.addOptions(options); // Options are { value, text }, Tom Select's default valueField and labelField
            },
        },
    }, overrides);
}

Not tested by the library: bootstrap-select 1.13 needs jQuery 3 or older.

import { mergeField } from './merge-field.js';

/**
 * A select Field shown as a bootstrap-select Widget (https://developer.snapappointments.com/bootstrap-select/),
 * created before makeForm with `$(select).selectpicker()`. bootstrap-select 1.13 needs jQuery 3 or older.
 * - It dispatches DOM `change` events on the <select>, which the Standard Behaviour of io.listen hears.
 * - It doesn't notice what the library writes in the <select>: after each write, `refresh` reads it again.
 */
export function bootstrapSelectField(name, overrides = {}) {
    const refresh = (htmlElement) => $(htmlElement).selectpicker('refresh');
    return mergeField({
        name,
        io: {
            set: (htmlElement, _value, standard) => {
                standard();
                refresh(htmlElement);
            },
        },
        behavior: {
            clear: (htmlElement, standard) => {
                standard();
                refresh(htmlElement);
            },
        },
        select: {
            saveData: (htmlElement, _options, standard) => {
                standard();
                refresh(htmlElement);
            },
        },
    }, overrides);
}

Tested with flatpickr 4.6.

import { mergeField } from './merge-field.js';

/**
 * An input Field shown as a flatpickr Widget (https://flatpickr.js.org), created before makeForm with `flatpickr(input)`.
 * - flatpickr keeps the input value in sync and dispatches DOM `change` events: reading and listening need no hook.
 * - A value written in the input isn't shown in the calendar: writing and clearing go through its instance.
 * - Its clear() fires `change`: the library ignores the changes of a field while it writes it.
 */
export function flatpickrField(name, overrides = {}) {
    return mergeField({
        name,
        io: {
            set: (htmlElement, value) => {
                htmlElement[0]._flatpickr.setDate(value);
            },
        },
        behavior: {
            clear: (htmlElement) => {
                htmlElement[0]._flatpickr.clear();
            },
        },
    }, overrides);
}

docs.title: Custom elements
docs.text:
A form-associated custom element with the field name (e.g. <sl-select name="city">) is a field like the others. The library doesn't recognise it as a select, checkbox or radio, so it gets the standard behaviour of a generic input: its value is read and written, and its change is listened to.

A select-like custom element doesn't get the select's options loading: there's no remote call through fetch, postProcessData, saveData or clearOnParentVoid. Load and write its options in behavior.updateStatus, passing signal to the remote call.

In TypeScript, state the element type of the field:

import type { FieldConfiguration } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';
// SlSelect: the class of the custom element, imported from its library

const city: FieldConfiguration<SlSelect, string> = {
    name: 'city',
    behavior: {
        updateStatus: async (htmlElement, data, subjectName, signal) => {
            const cities: { id: string, name: string }[] = await (await fetch(`/cities?country=${data.country}`, { signal })).json();
            htmlElement[0].replaceChildren(...cities.map((c) => Object.assign(document.createElement('sl-option'), { value: c.id, textContent: c.name })));
        },
    },
};

docs.title: Single Update Rule configuration
docs.text:
These rules declare which Observers to update when a Subject changes.

const updateRuleConfiguration = {
    name: 'fieldName',
    update: [],  // Names of the Observers to update when the Subject changes
    additionalData: [], // Names of other fields whose values go in the Update Data
    externalData: (data, subjectName) => { } // Function which returns external data to add to the Update Data
};

docs.title: name*
docs.text: The name of the Subject.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
The names of the Observers to update when the Subject changes. Their own Observers are cleared on cascade, since their value is no longer valid.

Update Rules can't form a cycle: a field can't be an Observer of itself, directly or through other fields. makeForm throws Update rules form a cycle: a → b → a when they do.

docs.title: additionalData
docs.text: The names of other fields whose values are read and added to the Update Data.

docs.title: externalData (data, subjectName)
docs.text:
A function to add to the Update Data other data, external to the form (e.g. a timestamp).

Parameters

  • {object} data: the Update Data collected so far, with the Subject's value and the additionalData values
  • {string} subjectName: the name of the Subject

Returns

  • {object} An object with external data values (key-value format)

docs.title: Update Data
docs.text:
The data an Observer receives for an update, keyed by field name: the Subject's value, plus the values of the additionalData fields and the object returned by externalData.

Field Hooks, fetch.makeUrl, fetch.makeBody and fetch.fullFetchConfig receive it as data.

docs.title: Contribute
docs.text:
Help me develop DynamicForms!

Remember to work on src/*.ts files, and test them building the bundle and importing it (import { makeForm } from '@dist/dynamic-forms.js'; for prod build, import { makeForm } from '@'; for dev mode).

Building needs Node 22.18 or later (see .nvmrc: nvm use).

Useful commands:

  • npm run dev - Start Vite server for local development
  • npm run build - Build DynamicForms library in dist folder with tsdown (see tsdown.config.ts)
  • npm test - Run the test suite once
  • npm run test:watch - Run the test suite in watch mode
  • npm run coverage - Run the test suite with a coverage report in coverage folder
  • npm run typecheck - Check types of sources and tests
  • npm run test:package - Build, pack and test the package as users load it: import and require in Node, a <script> tag, a Vite bundle; and that its declarations match its exports, its sourcemaps and declaration maps lead to src, and its JS files start with the banner
  • npm run lint:package - Check the package metadata and its types with publint and @arethetypeswrong/cli (after a build)
  • npm run size - Check the bundle sizes and that bundlers tree-shake the ES module build, with size-limit (after a build; budgets in .size-limit.json)

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Tests live in the tests folder and run with Vitest in a jsdom environment, which simulates the browser DOM inside Node.

  • Test through the public API (makeForm, getForm and the returned DynamicForm) on a real html form mounted with mountForm (see tests/helpers.ts)
  • Never call the network: stub remote calls with stubFetch
  • Known bugs are tracked with it.fails tests describing the expected behavior: fixing the bug makes them fail, so turn them into plain it tests

The CI runs typecheck and tests on every push and pull request on main, and before publishing a release.

Please, update also the documentation if you change anything.

Thank you very much for your support ❤

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
DynamicForms is build considered some use-cases I faced in my career.

It is a very generic library but there may be other use cases which I didn't account for. In this case please let me know, we can work together in implementing new features.

docs.title: Issues/Suggestions
docs.text:
If you have trouble using DynamicForms open an issue, I'll be glad to help you. Suggestions are also welcome!

It will be useful if you pass me some code to try: you can use tools like CodePen, PasteBin etc.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
Here is the UML Class Diagram to help you understand the project structure. Types are not specified for space reasons: the diagram is created using Mermaid which places elements automatically.

classDiagram

    class DynamicForm {
        ResolvedFormConfiguration config
        HTMLFormElement htmlElement
        Map❬String DynamicElement❭ entities
        boolean debug
        boolean enabled
        json elementToClassMapping

        +ready() Promise❬void❭
        +notify(subjectName) Promise❬void❭
        -fetchAllParameters(rule) UpdateData
        -clearCascade(currentSubject) Promise❬void❭
        +manualUpdate(data, subjectName) Promise❬void❭
        +destroy() void
        -getField(name) DynamicElement
        +getId() string
        +setEnabled() void
        +isEnabled() boolean
    }

    class dynamicForms {
        -Map❬String DynamicForm❭ formCollection
        +makeForm(formConfiguration) DynamicForm
        +getForm(id) DynamicForm
    }

    note for dynamicForms "Library entrypoint"

    class resolveConfiguration {
        +resolveConfiguration(formHtmlElement, formConfiguration) ResolvedFormConfiguration
    }

    note for resolveConfiguration "Checks the configuration and completes every Form and Field default, Discovered Fields included"

    class FieldBuilder {
        +createFieldsMap(fieldsCollection, htmlForm)
    }

    class DynamicElement {
        -ResolvedFieldConfiguration config
        -NodeList htmlElement
        -string name
        +get() string
        +set(value) string
        +clear()
        +update(data, subjectName)
        #canUpdate(data, subjectName) boolean
        #standardGet() string
        #standardSet(value)
        #standardClear()
        #standardUpdateStatus(data, subjectName) Promise❬void❭
    }

    note for DynamicElement "Public methods use the Field Hook if given, else the standard behaviour; subclasses override only the standard behaviours"

    class DynamicSelect {
        -string method
        #canUpdate(data, subjectName) boolean
        #standardClear()
        #standardUpdateStatus(data, subjectName, signal) Promise❬void❭
        -remoteCall(data, signal) Promise❬any❭
        #postProcessData(data) SelectOption[]
        #saveData(data) void
    }

    dynamicForms --> resolveConfiguration
    dynamicForms --> FieldBuilder

    DynamicForm <-- dynamicForms
    DynamicForm o-- DynamicElement

    DynamicElement <|-- DynamicSelect
    DynamicElement <|-- DynamicCheckbox
    DynamicElement <|-- DynamicRadio

docs.title: Cool computer science stuff
docs.text:
• DynamicForms is a particular instance of the Observer Design Pattern in which Subjects and Observers are all of the same type: form fields. The Observers don't register themselves: the Update Rules declare which fields observe which, and the Form, a Mediator between the fields, updates the Observers of each changed field. It works like a spreadsheet, where formulas declare which cells depend on which and the engine recomputes the cells depending on a changed one
  • The function used for the Cascade Clear (clearing fields on cascade) is the Depth-first search (DFS) used in Graph theory
  • The library entry point (src/index.js) implements the Facade Design Pattern to improve software usability: it masks more complex underlying code e.g. explicit objects instantiation and configuration fixing

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Dynamic-forms follows the semver standard.

docs.title: 4.0.0 (unreleased)
docs.text:
• Breaking: form.notify() rejects when a select's remote call fails, instead of logging the error and resolving. form.ready() rejects too when an initialisation remote call fails (#27). Changes triggered by the user still log the error to the console
  • form.ready() rejects when initialisation fails (e.g. beforeInit throws), instead of never settling (#28)
  • Breaking: every Field Hook receives the NodeList of the elements with the field name, even when there is only one. Hooks on single elements read htmlElement[0].value instead of htmlElement.value. Before, checkbox and radio io.get, io.set and behavior.clear and select behavior.updateStatus, postProcessData and saveData always received the NodeList, while the other hooks received the element itself when only one had the field name
  • Breaking (TypeScript): public types reworked so configurations need no casts. The package now exports FormConfiguration, FormHooks, UpdateRule, InitialisationRule, FieldConfiguration, FieldIoHooks, FieldFetchConfiguration, FieldHooks, SelectConfiguration, CheckboxConfiguration, UpdateData and the DynamicForm type
    • FormConfiguration requires only id, and behavior accepts any subset of the Form Hooks
    • FieldConfiguration has the select and checkbox keys; the former SelectConfiguration/CheckboxConfiguration interfaces extending it are gone, and the names now belong to the former SelectSelectConfiguration/CheckboxCheckboxConfiguration
    • Renamed FormBehavior to FormHooks, FieldBehaviorConfiguration to FieldHooks, FieldIoConfiguration to FieldIoHooks
    • The data received by Field Hooks, makeUrl, makeBody and externalData is UpdateData (Record<string, any>) instead of object, so data.country needs no annotation
    • Form Hooks and externalData receive a string Subject name, never null
    • Field Hooks receive NodeListOf<FieldElement> (FieldElement is HTMLInputElement | HTMLSelectElement | HTMLTextAreaElement) instead of HTMLElement | NodeList, so htmlElement[0].value needs no narrowing or cast. FieldConfiguration<E, V> states the element and value types of a field (FieldConfiguration<HTMLSelectElement>, FieldConfiguration<HTMLInputElement, string[]>); the value stays any by default
    • select.postProcessData receives the response as any and returns SelectOption[] ({ value: string | number, text: string }), which select.saveData receives
    • InitialisationRule.value is unknown instead of any
    • The behavior.afterUpdate Field Hook returns void instead of boolean: its result was never used
    • Exports FieldElement and SelectOption too
  • Breaking: fetch.fullFetchConfig is a function of the Update Data, (data) => RequestInit, instead of a static object, as the documentation already described (#31). Wrap an existing object as fullFetchConfig: () => ({ ... })
  • makeForm() no longer modifies the given configuration: defaults and discovered fields go into an internal copy. Form Hooks set to undefined fall back to the default instead of throwing
  • Breaking: makeForm() throws when the Update Rules form a cycle, including a field listing itself in its own update, which used to be ignored (#38). A cycle used to clear the field the user had just changed
  • Breaking: a custom behavior.beforeUpdate on a select no longer switches off select.clearOnParentVoid: with an empty Subject's value the select is cleared and its update stops before the hook is called (#40). Set clearOnParentVoid: false to handle an empty Subject's value in the hook
  • Breaking: makeForm() throws when the configuration mentions a name which is not a field of the form: in an Update Rule (its name, update or additionalData) or in an Initialisation Rule. These used to fail at the first update with Unknown element, or be silently ignored (#45). The error lists every unknown name, and every missing name; a Field Configuration for a missing field joins the list instead of throwing Element ... not found
  • Breaking: makeForm() throws when a Form for that id already exists, instead of leaving the previous one listening to the fields with its old configuration (#47). The new form.destroy() removes the Form's listeners, unregisters it from getForm() and aborts its remote calls; a pending notify(), manualUpdate() or ready() rejects with Form "id" was destroyed, as do later calls. Fields added after makeForm() are picked up by destroying the Form and creating it again
  • The behavior.updateStatus Field Hook receives a 4th parameter, the AbortSignal aborted when the Form is destroyed. A signal returned by fetch.fullFetchConfig is combined with it
  • Breaking: a failed remote call rejects notify() and ready() with a RemoteCallError, an Error exported by the package with the url and status in its message and the Response in error.response, instead of rejecting with the Response itself (#49). Read error.response.status instead of error.status
  • New select.loadOptions Field Hook: it replaces only the remote call of a select, receiving the parameters of updateStatus, and its data goes through postProcessData and saveData as usual (#50)
  • Breaking: the package is "type": "module" and its files are renamed: dist/dynamic-forms.js (ES module), dist/dynamic-forms.umd.cjs (UMD for require) and dist/dynamic-forms.umd.js (the same UMD for <script> tags and CDNs). exports gives each of import and require its own types, so the types resolve with every TypeScript moduleResolution (before, only with the deprecated node), and exports ./package.json and ./dist/*. The browser field is removed; unpkg and jsdelivr keep the bare CDN URL serving the UMD build. publint and @arethetypeswrong/cli check the package in CI, and npm run test:package tests the packed package with import and require in Node, as a <script> tag in jsdom and bundled by Vite (#52)
  • The package is built with tsdown instead of Vite (#54):
    • The sourcemaps map to the right lines of the TypeScript source (they were 6 lines off), and the new declaration maps make "Go to definition" open the TypeScript source in src
    • The types no longer declare a DynamicForm value: DynamicForm is a type-only export, as it always was at runtime, so x instanceof DynamicForm is a compile error instead of a runtime one
    • Bundlers tree-shake the ES module build: importing only RemoteCallError no longer bundles the whole library. The ES module build isn't minified any more (consumers' bundlers minify it); the UMD builds still are
    • Breaking: supported browsers are stated: Chrome and Edge 111+, Firefox 114+, Safari 16.4+, which is also the build target (the README said "works on all browsers"). A signal returned by fetch.fullFetchConfig works where the browser lacks AbortSignal.any
    • size-limit checks the bundle sizes and tree-shaking in CI
  • Third-party widgets (select2, Choices.js, Tom Select, bootstrap-select, flatpickr, form-associated custom elements) can be integrated through Field Hooks (#57), with a new Third-party widgets page and tested recipes:
    • New io.listen(htmlElement, onChange, standard) Field Hook: it subscribes to the field's changes and returns the function which unsubscribes, called by form.destroy(). It hears widgets that announce changes only through jQuery events or callbacks, which io.event never could
    • Every Field Hook which replaces a Standard Behaviour receives it as its last parameter, standard: io.listen, io.get, io.set, behavior.clear, behavior.updateStatus, select.loadOptions, select.postProcessData and select.saveData. Call it to add to the Standard Behaviour instead of rewriting it
    • Breaking: while the library writes to a field (io.set, behavior.clear, select.saveData), it ignores the changes that field fires: a hook or widget firing change when written no longer starts a second, duplicate update of the field's Observers
    • FieldConfiguration<E> accepts any HTMLElement, so a custom element's type can be stated
  • The loading docs cover every way to load the library: a bundler (import or require), a <script> tag from a CDN (with the DynamicForms global, and with Subresource Integrity), ES modules from esm.sh, an import map without a bundler, and self-hosting. CDN snippets use @4 instead of @latest, and the snippets that didn't work are fixed
  • Initialisation no longer clears the initial value of a field reached by the Cascade Clear of another initialised field (#37)
  • An update clears the Observers' Observers before updating the Observers, so the result no longer depends on the order of the names in update
  • form.notify() and form.ready() reject when clearing the Observers' Observers fails (e.g. a behavior.clear Field Hook throws), instead of leaving an unhandled rejection
  • Clearing a checkbox unchecks it instead of checking it (#25)
  • A select filled by a remote call gets an empty option when neither the html nor the data have one (#26). An option with value 0 is not taken for the empty one

• Webpack has been replaced with Vite
  • Library import does not expose the dynamicForms module anymore but makeform and getForm functions directly

• Library has been rewritten in typescript
  • FieldConfiguration.dropdown renamed to FieldConfiguration.select
  • Better documentation
• Added automatic field discovery: you don't need to specify fields with standard behavior anymore

• Supported fields initialisation
  • Added form.ready() method to synchronise post-initialisation operations
• Added support for nested input names (link). Thanks to @yoannisj
• First release

docs.title: Using a package manager (recommended)
docs.text:
npmYarnpnpm 
npm i @simomosi/dynamic-forms

yarn add @simomosi/dynamic-forms

pnpm i @simomosi/dynamic-forms

The package includes its TypeScript types, for every moduleResolution.

docs.title: Using a CDN or your own server
docs.text: Nothing to install: load the library in the page from a CDN, or download its files and serve them yourself. See Loading the library.

docs.title: Supported browsers
docs.text: Chrome and Edge 111+, Firefox 114+ and Safari 16.4+ (iOS 16.4+): the browsers "Baseline widely available" at the 4.0.0 release. No polyfills are needed.

docs.title: Loading the library
docs.text: Choose the way that fits your project. Load the library once per page: two copies would each keep their own forms, and getForm of one copy doesn't see the forms of the other.

docs.title: With a bundler
docs.text:
Vite, webpack, Rollup, esbuild and the other bundlers resolve the package installed with a package manager.

ES module (recommended)CommonJS 
import { makeForm } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';

const { makeForm } = require('@simomosi/dynamic-forms');

import loads the ES module build and require the UMD build: use one of the two in the whole app, since mixing them loads the library twice.

docs.title: From a CDN
docs.text: @4 follows the 4.x releases without jumping to a future major version, which could break your configuration. To freeze a release, write the exact version (e.g. @4.0.0). Avoid @latest.

docs.title: Script tag
docs.text:
The script defines the global variable DynamicForms.

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4"></script>
<script>
    const { makeForm } = DynamicForms;
</script>

https://unpkg.com/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4 serves the same file.

docs.title: Script tag with Subresource Integrity
docs.text:
With Subresource Integrity the browser runs the script only if it is exactly the published file. It needs an exact version and the full file path:

<script
    src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4.0.0/dist/dynamic-forms.umd.js"
    integrity="sha384-REPLACED_AT_THE_4.0.0_RELEASE"
    crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

For another version, take the hash from the version's page on jsDelivr, or compute it:

curl -s https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4.0.0/dist/dynamic-forms.umd.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A

docs.title: ES module
docs.text:
<script type="module">
    import { makeForm } from 'https://esm.sh/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4';
</script>

esm.sh also sends the TypeScript types (useful with Deno). https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4/+esm works too.

docs.title: Without a bundler: import map
docs.text:
In a plain html page, import ... from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms' works only with an import map, which tells the browser where the package is. Without it (or a bundler, or a dev server like Vite's) the browser throws a TypeError.

<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": { "@simomosi/dynamic-forms": "https://esm.sh/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4" } }
</script>
<script type="module">
    import { makeForm } from '@simomosi/dynamic-forms';
</script>

docs.title: Self-hosting
docs.text:
To serve the library from your own site, copy one of these files from the npm package (node_modules/@simomosi/dynamic-forms/dist/):

  • dynamic-forms.js: the ES module, for <script type="module"> and import maps;
  • dynamic-forms.umd.js: the UMD build, for a <script> tag (defines DynamicForms).
<script src="/js/dynamic-forms.umd.js"></script>
<!-- or -->
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": { "@simomosi/dynamic-forms": "/js/dynamic-forms.js" } }
</script>

Build scripts and copy plugins can find the files with require.resolve('@simomosi/dynamic-forms/dist/dynamic-forms.umd.js') or import.meta.resolve('@simomosi/dynamic-forms/dist/dynamic-forms.js').

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
Did you already installed and loaded the library? Then go on, you are almost there!

Let's assume we are working on the following html form:

<form id='form_id'>
    <label for="field_one">Field one</label>
    <select id="field_one" name='field_one'>
        <option value="" selected></option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
    </select>

    <label for="field_two">Field two</label>
    <select id="field_two" name='field_two'>
        <option value="" selected></option>
    </select>
</form>

Let's assume we loaded dynamic-forms using a CDN: 

<script type="module">
    import { makeForm } from 'https://esm.sh/@simomosi/dynamic-forms@4';
</script>

docs.title: Write the Form Configuration
docs.text:
For the Form Configuration we need to write 2 lists:

  1. fields: a list of the fields you want to customise (using the Field Configuration format); a field which loads its options from a remote url needs a Field Configuration;
  2. rules: a list of Update Rules, which tell the Observers to update when a Subject changes, usually on a change event (using the Update Rule format)
const formConfiguration = {
    id: 'form_id',
    fields: [
        {
            name: 'field_two',
            fetch: {
                makeUrl: (data) => `https://url/to/api/`,
            }
        }
    ],
    rules: [
        {
            name: 'field_one',
            update: ['field_two']
        },
    ]
};

Note: we didn't need to specify a Field Configuration for field_one: it is discovered automatically.

docs.title: Create the form
docs.text:
Create the form and forget about it: dynamic-forms will work by itself!

const form = makeForm(formConfiguration);

docs.title: Done!
docs.text:
Look at the network tab in developer console/tools while you play with your form!

Of course you need a real api-endpoint to load your values. For a working example open files in the example folder in your browser.

This is a basic configuration which works with default values. To customize it to your needs check the documentation chapter.

docs.title: Tutorial - Set the Initial Status
docs.text:
Sometimes you need to load a prefilled form, and the initial values should trigger actions like retrieving data, hide or disable other fields.

Dynamic-forms can automatically set the form initial status and trigger those operations for you.

You need to list in the Initialisation Rules all the fields which require the initialisation, describing:

  1. Their name
  2. Their initial value (optional)
const formConfiguration = {
    id: 'form_id',
    fields:[/* ... */],
    rules: [/* ... */],
    init: [
        {
            name: 'field_one',
            value: '1'
        },
    ]
};

Note: you need to specify an API-endpoint in fields for field_one to work.

Dynamic-forms uses:

  • the Field Configurations in the fields section to retrieve remote data for each field listed in the Initialisation Rules (init section)
  • the Update Rules in the rules section to update the Observers of the initialised fields

In the example above, dynamic-forms will first initialise field_one using its Field Configuration and its Initialisation Rule, then it will update its Observer field_two using the Update Rules specified in the previous page.

If you need to pass other data to the initialised fields, just list their name and value in the Initialisation Rules (init collection) just like they were form fields: they go in the Update Data.

docs.title: Wait for complete initialisation
docs.text:
The initialisation phase is an asynchronous procedure: your script will continue without waiting for the subroutine to end.

If you need to execute code after the initialisation is complete, use the ready function as shown below.

PromiseAsync/Await 
const form = makeForm(formConfiguration);
form.ready().then(() => {
    /* Your code here */
});

async function initialiseForm() {
    let form = makeForm(formConfiguration);
    await form.ready();
    /* Your code here */
}
initialiseForm();
